title: Cow's milk protein allergy in babies
what: A small amount of blood is taken from your baby to check for antibodies to cow's milk proteins. It is one clue for the doctor, not a final answer.
why: If your baby gets a rash, vomiting, diarrhea, blood in the stool, or is very fussy after formula or dairy foods.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 to 10 minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: What your baby ate and when before the reaction, and what it looked like
How you feed now: breast milk, formula, or solid foods
If your baby takes allergy medicine or uses steroid creams
If parents, brothers, or sisters have allergies
If there were severe reactions: swelling or trouble breathing

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Your baby usually does not need to fast. Feed as usual, unless the lab says otherwise.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. If your baby takes allergy medicine, tell the doctor. They will decide.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write down what your baby ate and any reactions. You can take photos of the rash.

prepare.title: Comfort
prepare.text: Bring a favorite toy, bottle, or pacifier. It helps your baby stay calm.

bring: The food diary and photos of reactions
steps: You hold your baby or stay right next to them
The nurse finds a vein in the arm, sometimes on the back of the hand
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood goes into a small tube
A cotton pad and a bandage are put on the spot
feel: Babies almost always cry. It is from fright and the prick, not from strong pain
You can pick up and feed your baby right away
after: Hold the cotton pad on for a few minutes
Results usually come in a few days
Even a normal result does not rule out allergy. Some types do not show up in the blood
Your doctor decides how to feed your baby next. Do not change feeding suddenly without them
red_flags: Swelling of the face or lips, wheezing, or trouble breathing after dairy: call emergency services
Your baby is floppy, pale, or vomiting a lot: see a doctor right away or call emergency services

faq.q: If the test is normal, does that mean no allergy?
faq.a: Not always. Some milk allergies happen without antibodies in the blood. The doctor looks at the test together with how your baby reacts to food.

faq.q: Should a breastfeeding mother cut out dairy?
faq.a: Your doctor decides. Do not go on a strict diet on your own. You could miss foods you need.

reminders.text: Your baby's milk allergy blood test is tomorrow. Bring the food diary, a bottle, and a toy.
